title: Separable States Violate the Complementary-Quantum Correlation Conjecture
authors: Jinbo Wang, Qihang Wang, Kun Chen
abstract: Correlations measured in complementary local bases provide an experimentally accessible probe of the total correlations in a bipartite quantum state. The complementary-quantum correlation conjecture asserts that the sum of two such classical mutual informations never exceeds the premeasurement quantum mutual information. We disprove this conjecture in every local dimension $d\geq3$ with an explicit rank-two separable state. One of the two complementary measurements recovers the complete one-bit branch label, while the other retains additional classical correlation. For qutrits the excess is exactly $\frac13\log_2(3456/3125)=0.0484156759\ldots$ bits. Continuity yields full-rank separable violations. The effect therefore requires neither entanglement nor quantum discord; it arises from two complementary readouts of the same classical latent variable.
summary: The paper disproves the Complementary-Quantum Correlation conjecture using an explicit, non-entangled (separable) state for local dimensions $d \geq 3$. By comparing classical mutual information sums from complementary measurements against the quantum mutual information, the authors demonstrate a measurable excess. This finding is significant because it shows that correlations violating this bound do not require entanglement or quantum discord.
main_problem: The paper aims to disprove the Complementary-Quantum Correlation (CQC) conjecture, which posits an upper bound on the sum of classical mutual informations from complementary measurements relative to the quantum mutual information.
main_result: The CQC conjecture is disproved for all local dimensions $d \geq 3$ using a specific rank-two separable state. This violation occurs even without invoking entanglement or quantum discord.
method: The authors analyze the bipartite state using two complementary projective measurements (computational and Fourier-conjugate bases) and calculate classical Shannon mutual informations to show their sum exceeds the premeasurement quantum mutual information.
model_or_system: The study considers a general bipartite quantum state $ho_{AB}$ defined for local dimension $d \geq 3$. The counterexample specifically utilizes an explicit rank-two separable state: $ho_{AB} =  rac{1}{2}|uangle\langle u|_A \otimes |vangle\langle v|_B +  rac{1}{2}|vangle\langle v|_A \otimes |uangle\langle u|_B$.
key_observables: Classical mutual informations $I(Z_A : Z_B)$ and $I(X_A : X_B)$, compared against the quantum mutual information $I(A:B)$. The excess violation is quantified for qutrits as $\approx 0.048$ bits.
important_parameters: Local dimension $d \geq 3$. The violation persists and approaches a limit as $d 	o \infty$.
main_assumptions: The counterexample state is separable, meaning the failure of the conjecture occurs in non-entangled regimes. The result only refutes the specific two-sided CQC inequality.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the CQC conjecture and then constructs a concrete counterexample using a separable state for $d \geq 3$. It calculates the relevant mutual information quantities to demonstrate the violation, concluding with the physical interpretation that the effect stems from complementary readouts of a shared classical variable.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental theoretical challenge to existing bounds in quantum correlation theory by showing that simple separable states can violate conjectures previously thought to hold universally, impacting how we quantify non-classical correlations.
